styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old Town lanes, the cathedral and world-class museums.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Lake cruises, lakeside promenades and Alpine day trips.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Fondue, lake fish and chocolate shops.

stays.why: Steps from the cathedral, museums and the lake; quiet at night but hilly cobbled lanes.
Central and lively, close to the station and the lake; many budget hotels and cheap eats.
Leafy and local, near the lake beaches and parks; good for families and longer stays.
Student and arts quarter with a flea market; tram links to both banks, good value.

food: Try fondue or raclette in the Old Town; portions are big, so share one between two.
Lake fish (perch fillets, 'filets de perche') is a local favourite; ask for the day's catch.
Cheap eats: Pâquis has kebab shops, falafel and Asian cafeterias, roughly CHF 10–20 a meal.
Pick up bread, cheese and fruit at a market or supermarket for a picnic by the lake; it saves a lot.
Restaurant prices are high. Lunch menus ('menu du jour') cost less than dinner; book popular places ahead.
more_time: Take a boat trip on Lake Geneva (Les Mouettes or CGN cruises) to see the city and the Alps from the water.
Swap a city afternoon for a day trip to Montreux or Lausanne by train; check times and prices on the day.
Cross into France for a cheaper lunch in Annemasse or a walk along the lake shore; bring your passport.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Old Town, museums and a lake cruise; add a night for an Alpine day trip.

month_notes: Cold and grey, highs near 5°C; pack a warm coat and expect some rain.
Still cold, highs around 8°C; a quiet month for museums.
Milder, highs near 11°C; rain is common, bring an umbrella.
Spring arrives, highs around 15°C; good for walking the lake shore.
Pleasant, highs near 18°C; one of the wetter months, keep a rain layer.
Warm and bright, highs around 24°C; long evenings by the lake.
Hottest month, highs near 27°C; book lake swims and shade.
Warm, highs around 26°C; a great month for the lake and parks.
Mild and pleasant, highs near 21°C; fewer rain days than spring.
Cooler, highs around 16°C; autumn colours and quieter streets.
Chilly, highs near 10°C; rain is frequent, dress in layers.
Cold, highs around 7°C; festive season, short daylight.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate lakeside climate: cold, grey winters and warm, sunny summers, with rain spread across the year.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Highs of 24–27°C and the most sun. Ideal for the lake, parks and boat trips.

items.title: Winter is cold (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 5–8°C and lows near 0°C. Pack a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 9–14 rain days most months. Bring a light waterproof and an umbrella.

items.title: Spring warms up slowly
items.text: March to May climbs from 11°C to 18°C. Pleasant but changeable; layer up.

items.title: Mild autumn
items.text: September and October stay around 16–21°C; good for walking before the cold sets in.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobbled lanes; sunglasses and sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Trams and buses with a TPG ticket, or a free transport card from your hotel.

modes.text: No metro. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
TPG trams and buses cover most of the city. Buy a ticket at the stop machine before boarding: about CHF 3 for one hour, CHF 8 for a day pass.
Metered taxis are pricey; Uber and similar apps operate in Geneva.
Possible, but parking is costly and the centre is compact. Use transit instead for city trips.
The city is fairly flat and good for walking and bikes. Genèveroule lends bikes free in summer.
Yellow 'mouette' boats cross the lake and are covered by TPG tickets.
